chains.title: GABPA binding at the alt allele activates TERT

links.claim: GABPA is predicted to bind the alt A allele more strongly. GABPA has its own QBiC-SELEX model at this base with an alt-favoring change (effect 4.05, z 71.32; E33), and a second shared ETS model also favors alt (E17). GABPA is expressed in glioblastoma (15.52 TPM; E17), and ENCODE GABPA peaks contain the variant only in other biosamples, HepG2 and SK-N-SH, not glioblastoma (E32; E17). No ENCODE biosample matches the glioblastoma expression context (E04), so occupancy at this base in the disease context is not demonstrated. GABPA is preferred over FLI1/ETV2/ETV3 because it has an own-model QBiC-SELEX result, higher glioblastoma expression, and literature support for GABP at mutant TERT promoters (E33, E17, E34); the other ETS factors rely only on the shared ETV5-mapped model.

The variant lies in the active promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS) with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal and in the annotated TERT promoter. The cCRE activity z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific.
The element is immediately upstream of TERT (0 kb from the TERT TSS), so an allelic change in TF binding at this base is predicted to alter TERT transcription.

Glioblastoma is a plausible expression context because GABPA is expressed in glioblastoma lines and the element has promoter-like marks, but direct GABPA occupancy at this base in glioblastoma is not shown; ENCODE has no matching glioblastoma GABPA ChIP signal at the variant (E32), and the cCRE marks are not biosample-specific for glioblastoma.

If alt-enhanced GABPA binding activates the TERT promoter, increased TERT/telomerase activity is predicted to promote TERT promoter mutant cancers. Literature includes a study on GABP coupling oncogene signaling to telomere regulation in TERT promoter mutant cancer (E34), and generic TERT-disease literature links TERT to glioblastoma/melanoma (E15). Direct C250T-specific allele assays are not provided, and bladder-cancer support is not direct in the cited titles.

predictions: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP in a C250T-heterozygous glioblastoma cell line shows more GABPA on the alt A allele than on the ref G allele at this base.
An alt-allele TERT promoter reporter shows higher activity than the ref allele, and GABPA knockdown reduces this difference.
GABPA depletion reduces TERT expression preferentially in cells carrying the alt allele.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP in a C250T-heterozygous glioblastoma line shows no alt>ref occupancy at this base.
GABPA knockdown or depletion does not reduce alt-associated TERT expression or reporter activity.
The alt allele does not increase TERT expression in an allele-specific, GABPA-dependent manner in glioblastoma cells.

predictions: No allele-specific TF occupancy at this base explains the disease association.

TERT expression is not consistently altered by this base in an allele-specific manner beyond linked variant effects.

The alt allele changes TERT expression in an allele-specific manner in a relevant cell type.

chains.title: Loss of KLF12 repressor binding on the alt allele

links.claim: KLF12 is predicted to bind the ref G allele more strongly, but the evidence is weak. QBiC-SELEX detects a ref-favoring change (z -15.38, effect -0.439; E18), yet the best model is a CIS-BP-mapped KLF5 model rather than a KLF12-specific model. ENCODE KLF12 occupancy over the variant is only in HepG2, not glioblastoma (E18), and KLF12 is expressed at a low level in glioblastoma lines (4.47 TPM, rank 787; E18).
The variant lies in the active promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS) and in the annotated TERT promoter; activity marks are maxima over biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific.
The element is immediately upstream of TERT (0 kb from the TERT TSS), placing a predicted KLF12 site in the TERT promoter region.
KLF12 cell-type support is weak: KLF12 is expressed in glioblastoma lines but at low level, and its only occupancy evidence over this variant is from HepG2; no glioblastoma KLF12 occupancy is shown.

If KLF12 normally repressed TERT, loss of KLF12 binding on the alt allele could derepress TERT and promote tumor growth. However, no cited evidence establishes that KLF12 represses TERT, so this phenotype step is speculative.

predictions: Allele-specific KLF12 ChIP shows stronger KLF12 binding on the ref G allele than on the alt A allele.
The alt allele increases TERT reporter activity specifically when KLF12 is present.
falsified_if: Allele-specific KLF12 ChIP does not show ref>alt binding at this base in a relevant cell type.
KLF12 depletion does not increase TERT expression.
The alt allele does not derepress TERT in a KLF12-dependent manner.

chains.title: NR2C1 binding at the alt allele activates TERT

links.claim: NR2C1 is predicted to bind the alt A allele more strongly, but the evidence is weak. QBiC-SELEX detects an alt-favoring change (z 15.31, effect 1.182; E19), yet the best model is a CIS-BP-mapped RORC model, not a clearly NR2C1-specific model. ENCODE NR2C1 occupancy over the variant is only in GM12878, not glioblastoma (E19). NR2C1 is expressed in glioblastoma lines (18.52 TPM, rank 251; E19).
The variant lies in the active promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS) and in the annotated TERT promoter; activity marks are maxima over biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific.
The element is immediately upstream of TERT (0 kb from the TERT TSS), placing a predicted NR2C1 site in the TERT promoter region.

NR2C1 cell-type support is weak: NR2C1 is expressed in glioblastoma lines, but its occupancy evidence over this variant is from GM12878 only; no glioblastoma NR2C1 occupancy or function at this element is demonstrated.

If NR2C1 activated the TERT promoter, alt-enhanced NR2C1 binding could increase TERT expression and promote tumor growth. However, no cited evidence establishes that NR2C1 activates TERT, so this phenotype step is speculative.

predictions: Allele-specific NR2C1 ChIP shows stronger NR2C1 binding on the alt A allele than on the ref G allele in glioblastoma cells.
NR2C1 knockdown reduces TERT expression preferentially from the alt allele.
The alt allele increases TERT reporter activity in an NR2C1-dependent manner.
falsified_if: Allele-specific NR2C1 ChIP does not show alt>ref binding at this base in glioblastoma cells.
NR2C1 depletion does not reduce mutant TERT expression.
The alt allele does not increase TERT in an NR2C1-dependent manner.

chains.title: Alternative ETS factor FLI1 binds the alt allele

links.claim: FLI1 is predicted to bind the alt A allele more strongly only through the shared ETV5-mapped ETS QBiC-SELEX model (z 167.5, effect 2.421; E29). This model is identical for GABPA/ETV2/ETV3/FLI1 and does not distinguish FLI1 from other ETS factors. FLI1 has unknown ENCODE occupancy at this base and low glioblastoma expression (4.71 TPM, rank 767; E29).
The variant lies in the active promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS) and in the annotated TERT promoter; activity marks are maxima over biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific.
The element is immediately upstream of TERT (0 kb from the TERT TSS), so an alt-favoring ETS site here could affect TERT transcription.
FLI1 cell-type support is weak: FLI1 is expressed at low level in glioblastoma lines, has unknown occupancy at this base, and no glioblastoma FLI1 ChIP evidence is given.

If FLI1 activated the TERT promoter, alt-enhanced FLI1 binding could increase TERT expression and promote tumor growth. However, no cited evidence establishes that FLI1 activates TERT, so this phenotype step is speculative.

predictions: Allele-specific FLI1 ChIP shows stronger FLI1 binding on the alt A allele than on the ref G allele in glioblastoma cells.
FLI1 knockdown reduces TERT expression in cells carrying the alt allele.
The alt allele increases ETS-dependent TERT reporter activity that is not explained by GABPA.
falsified_if: No ETS-family occupancy is detected at this base in glioblastoma cells.
FLI1 is not expressed or not bound at this promoter in glioblastoma cells.
The alt allele does not increase TERT in an ETS-dependent manner.

grades_v0.reason: QBiC-SELEX reports an alt-favoring change (E17), but the best model is a CIS-BP-mapped ETV5 ETS model shared with ETV2/ETV3/FLI1 (E27-E29), so it does not specifically establish GABPA binding. ENCODE GABPA peaks contain the variant only in other biosamples (HepG2, SK-N-SH; E11/E17), and E04 explicitly says no ENCODE biosample matches the expression context, so no relevant-cell-type occupancy is demonstrated. Binding evidence is therefore indirect/prediction-only.

Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap subtype median Glioblastoma), bound here before bound elsewhere, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 18 occupied, 5 of 145 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 0 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 554 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 1 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only.
